in_text_mentions: A three-month-old boy presented with a mass localised extra nasally on the left side of the root of the nose since birth (Figure 1). There was no history of epistaxis, nasal obstruction, breathing difficulties, or feeding difficulties. The swelling did not worsen in response to crying or obstruct his vision. The swelling was non-tender, non-pulsatile, non-discharging, and firm in consistency. It was non-compressible and non-reducible in response to pressure or posture. in_text_mentions: Histopathologically, the tumor consisted of neuroglial cells, neuroglial fibers, and vascularized connective tissue. The tumor was surrounded by normal respiratory mucosa. The neuroglial cells were stained positive for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Coronal CT of a human patient from a case report titled 'A case of nasal glial heterotopia in an adult'; the caption directly attributes the isodense sinonasal mass without bony erosion to nasal glial heterotopia, matching the CT vocabulary finding. b: Coronal CT of the same human patient with an arrow marking the small cribriform plate defect described in the caption and in-text; shows a specific structural feature of the patient's nasal glial heterotopia.
panels.attribution_text: Hagiwara et al. A case of nasal glial heterotopia in an adult.. Case reports in otolaryngology 2014. doi:10.1155/2014/354672. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: CT showed an isodense mass which occupied the right nasal cavity, maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses, with no erosion of the bony walls. ↓: A small defect in the cribriform plate.
in_text_mentions: arin). Endoscopic examination revealed a soft, white, and polypoid mass that occluded the right nasal cavity (Figure 1). A computed tomography (CT) scan of the facial bones showed an isodense shadow, which occupied the right nasal cavity, maxillary, anterior ethmoid, and frontal sinuses, with no erosion of the bony walls (Figure 2). There was a small defect in the cribriform plate. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed that the tumor had high signal intensity surrounded by an isointense area on the T2-weighted image (Figure 3). No connection with the meninges or cerebral tissue was observed.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E (100x) of the excised nasal mass in a patient diagnosed with nasal glial heterotopia/nasal glioma; the caption and in-text describe a highly fibrotic hypocellular lesion. The panel is a real patient histology image of the target disease, but the depicted fibrosis/spindle-cell pattern is not represented by a controlled vocabulary key (no glial/astrocytic tissue is visible at this power), so the visible features are listed as proposed findings. The unusually fibrotic, storiform-like pattern is the reason the case can be misdiagnosed as sclerotic fibroma/collagenoma, hence 'variant'. B: High-power H&E (200x) of the same nasal glial heterotopia excision specimen, showing spindle cells and collagen bundles in a fascicular/whorled pattern without neuropil or ganglion cells. Real patient histology of the target disease; the described fibrotic stromal pattern is not in the controlled vocabulary, so it is captured as proposed...
panels.attribution_text: Gundogdu et al. A Case of Nasal Glial Heterotopia That Can Be Misdiagnosed as Storiform Patterned Sclerotic Fibroma/Collagenoma.. Turk patoloji dergisi 2024. doi:10.5146/tjpath.2023.13053. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: In the histopathological evaluation of the specimen, A) low power magnification shows a highly fibrotic hypocellular lesion (H&E 100x), B) high power magnification shows the lesion is composed of spindle cells and collagen bundles arranged in a fascicular and whorled pattern, and no neuropil or ganglion cells can be seen (H&E 200x). The glial tissue that was entrapped with fibrovascular stroma was positive for C) S100 and D) GFAP.
in_text_mentions: n of the excision material revealed a firm, white, nodular 1.6x1.3x0.8 cm lesion. Microscopically, a highly fibrotic hypocellular lesion was composed primarily of spindle cells and collagen bundles organized in a fascicular pattern (Figure 2). There were no apparent neuropil or ganglion cells with H&E (Figure 2). The glial tissue entrapped by a fibrovascular stroma was immunohistochemically positive for S100 (Figure 2) and GFAP (Figure 2), but negative for CD34 and EMA. Neu-N immunostaining revealed no neuronal cells. These findings led to the diagnosis of nasal glial heterotopia/nasal glioma.
